properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): one decision was kept in three places because hxm_program's own two checks each demand a copy: its file-home ratchet (DECISIONS.md) and its docs-graph coverage (an LLM-authored graph of the docs). The reason for the first is reflow2's. A reader who never runs reflow2 has no served surface for accepted decisions. A file linked to a Decision is never reported stale when the Decision moves, because propagation does not traverse DOCUMENTS. The need was recorded only as a lesson, after two earlier asks from the same hub were never recorded
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-28, reflow2 0.73.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. Item F-34.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "One decision, three bookkeeping surfaces. D-0021 (PR 88 scope) was written as: an `add_decision` node; a `DECISIONS.md` entry; a `docs-graph` node plus re-render. It was then revised in all three, for the same-day reversal. The file-home ratchet requires (2), and the docs-graph check requires (3). Each is justified alone; together they triple the cost of the most important kind of capture, and three copies can disagree." EXPECTED: one capture, with the other readers served from it. NOT AFFECTED: the design-side revise itself, which preserved the prior text (praised in the same report).

② PRECEDENT (search_design on the raw words): fact:lessons-from-hxm-program-the-first-reflow2-hub-for-the-hub-model-2026-09-23, lesson ②: "READERS WHO DO NOT RUN reflow2 NEED A FILE-SIDE HOME FOR BINDING CONTENT, AND hxm_program BUILT ONE ... reflow2 has no concept of a reader who does not use it." It was recorded as a lesson in a TemporalFact, not as an idea or a requirement. The same hub asked twice before: O-04 (2026-08-26: "export_markdown — accepted decisions, enforced rules, open questions rendered as the graph's published view" and "a detector — ... which accepted/enforced nodes are referenced by none of them") and O-08 (2026-09-10: "a DOCUMENTS-style edge ... would let reflow2 itself raise 'accepted decision with no document'"). Neither id appears anywhere in the design. fact:defect-propagate-change-is-silent-on-documents-and-cannot-say-why (2026-08-15). dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph (reflow2's OWN docs, open since 2026-08-11, option (e) link-ripple-rewrite added 2026-09-16). rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents (reflow2's own practice).

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) GOVERNANCE, the project's: hxm_program's own two rules each demand a copy.
(B) INTENT, reflow2's: the need of a reader who never runs reflow2 was never stated as intent, so no served surface exists and the project built its own.
(C) CHANGE: DOCUMENTS is not traversed by propagation, so even a linked decision log is not reported stale when a Decision is revised; only a hand-built check can notice.
(D) GRAIN: the file log and the design's decisions are different grains, so the "copy" is a curated summary that no rendering would remove.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: the three are not copies of one content.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: A predicts project rules naming both surfaces; B predicts no served read or render of decisions for a file and no Decision or Requirement holding the need; C predicts the propagation code skipping DOCUMENTS; D predicts file entries and accepted decisions far from 1:1; E predicts entries whose content differs from the nodes.

⑤ RESULTS (hxm_program checkout 77d2f1f, 2026-09-23, read-only; reflow2 v0.74.0 source):
· A HOLDS. D-0016 (AJ, 2026-08-25): "Only AJ runs reflow2, so ... every accepted decision / enforced rule / accepted requirement must have a file-side home (DECISIONS.md, an AGENTS.md rule line, or a dated block in the task file)", built into tools/check_repo.py as a ratchet. The same script's docs-graph check requires "every D-000N in DECISIONS.md ... should appear as a node in docs-graph/graph.json", and docs-graph/render.sh says graph.json "is produced by the LLM agent itself" and rendered with graphify. Surface (3) is entirely the project's own and derives from (2); reflow2 plays no part in it.
· B HOLDS. No served tool renders a Decision for a file; the only generated document is reflow2's own CHANGELOG. The phrase "who do not run reflow2" occurs in one node, the 09-23 lesson fact; no Decision or Requirement holds the need. The newly accepted req:the-agent-renders-the-design-for-the-reader-who-needs-it covers a view rendered on demand in a session, not a standing surface for a reader who never opens one.
· C HOLDS. crates/reflow2-core/src/artifact.rs:651: "PROPAGATE deliberately does not traverse `DOCUMENTS` yet". It is still live at v0.74.0, six weeks after the 08-15 defect.
· D HOLDS IN PART. hxm's design holds 85 Decisions, 66 accepted; DECISIONS.md holds 20 D-entries. Only 7 accepted decision ids appear in the file, because D-0016 also accepts "a D-NNNN its own text names" as a home. art:decisions-log (the file) carries one REALIZES to a Capability and ZERO DOCUMENTS edges, so the design cannot say which Decision a D-entry holds. The file is a coarser, curated log, linked by ids in prose that only hxm's script matches.
· E QUALIFIED. D-0016's entry bundles a decision, its progress and the affected artifacts, so entries are not pure copies. The reporter's point stands anyway: one reversal cost three edits.

⑥ CLASS: reflow2's own practice (design information lives in the graph, not in documents) was written for a project whose every reader runs reflow2. A consumer with readers who do not gets no served surface and no staleness signal, so it builds its own copy and its own check, and every capture pays for both. It also shows a recording gap: the need was asked twice (O-04, O-08) and recorded once, as a LESSON in a TemporalFact, which no loop reads as owed. Three sightings produced zero ideas. A fix at the class, a served surface or check for readers outside reflow2, would have answered O-04, O-08 and lesson ②. Removing hxm's docs-graph check would answer only today's third copy.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code was changed. A class-pinning test would assert three things. First, a Decision revised after a DOCUMENTS-linked file's baseline makes propagate_change name that file as owed a rewrite. Second, a served read can render the accepted decisions and enforced rules a file-side log needs. Third, for a project that opts in, an accepted Decision that no registered document reaches is reported.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: three surfaces, triple cost, copies can disagree. QUALIFIED: "the docs-graph check requires (3)" is hxm's own check over an LLM-authored graph of its docs; reflow2 cannot remove it, though a served surface for non-users could make the project's reason for it weaker. The file entries are coarser than the nodes, so "one decision, three copies" is closer to one decision, one node and one hand-written summary per bundle.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: D-0021 itself, which is after this checkout; whether hxm's colleagues read DECISIONS.md or the docs-graph more; the reporting machine's current check_repo.py, which may have moved since 2026-09-23.
